SMWMFL

* Special Marine Warning for...
Biscayne Bay...
Coastal waters from Deerfield Beach to Ocean Reef FL out 20 NM...

* Until 345 PM EDT.

* At 302 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Coral Gables, moving east at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts, wind gusts to nearly 50 knots, and small
hail.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Soldier Key, Key Biscayne, Biscayne Bay, Elliott Key, Black Point,

properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 3 at 9:17AM CDT until August 6 at 1:00PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...Until Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 37.3 feet, Widespread lowland flooding occurs. Minor
roads are closed. Airport Road boat ramp near Live Oak County
Airport is flooded and closed. Major flooding occurs in the River
Creek Acres Subdivision, with several feet of water and several
homes flooded. Residents in the J.I. Hailey Subdivision at Jones
River bend have trouble getting out as water covers much of
Antelope Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Monday the stage was 37.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall into moderate flood
stage Tuesday, then fall below flood stage midday Thursday. The
river will then continue to fall to 12.8 feet Saturday morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Portions of New Jersey, including the following counties,
Burlington, Camden and Mercer and southeast Pennsylvania,
including the following counties, Bucks, Delaware, Montgomery and
Philadelphia.

* WHEN...Until 515 PM EDT.

* IMPACTS...It will take several hours for all the water from these
storms to work through local drainage systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 305 PM EDT, reports of minor street flooding have occurred
across the I95 urban corridor. The rainfall producing this
street flooding is generally less than one half an inch but
is resulting from several waves of rainfall that have
occurred through the day today and no ability for the runoff
to drain. The street flooding is not expected to be as life
threatening as the flooding that occurred this morning but
does pose a threat to property. Doppler radar indicated heavy
rain. Between 1 and 4 inches of rain have fallen across the
storm total for today.
- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Philadelphia, Trenton, Camden, Bensalem, Ewing, Norristown,
Yeadon, Burlington, Bristol, Conshohocken, Palmyra and
Hatboro.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
